title: Stratified sampling guardrail and deferred fallback orchestrator
author: Omar Hassan
release_notes: Add stratified sampling probe scheduler with entropy-normalized cohorting; introduce deferred fallback orchestrator to reduce noisy rollbacks; config knobs for sampling budgets and stability escrow.
description: Context: we see frequent spurious rollbacks during gradual rollouts when small cohorts produce high-variance latency signals. This PR introduces a two-part solution: a stratified sampling guardrail that ensures probes sample across traffic modalities and an orchestrator that defers fallback decisions until an aggregated stability escrow is satisfied. Motivation: reduce noisy rollbacks and improve signal-to-noise for regression detection without adding significant probe traffic. Design summary: 1) Stratified sampler: samples requests into cohorts by three axes (route, tokenized length bucket, and tenant weight class). Sampling budget is enforced per-cohort and normalized by an entropy metric so low-variance cohorts get proportionally fewer probes. Rough pseudocode: func selectCohort(req) -> cohortID { /* routeHash % N, lengthBucket(req.length), tenantBucket(req.tenantWeight) */ } func shouldProbe(cohort) -> bool { /* uses budgetRemaining[cohort] and entropyNormalizer */ } 2) Deferred fallback orchestrator: when a canary metric crosses a threshold, instead of immediate rollback, we allocate a stability escrow (a short time window and probe budget) to confirm regression across cohorts and time slices. The orchestrator maintains decay-weighted evidence and only triggers fallback when evidence > configured quorum. This reduces churn from transient spikes. Key knobs: - per_cohort_budget (int) - entropy_normalizer_alpha (float) - escrow_window_seconds (int) - fallback_quorum_fraction (float) Backwards compatibility: default configs keep current sampling behavior; feature gated under canary.feature.stratified_sampling=true Migration: operator migration is a config toggle (no rolling restart required). Checklist: - [x] Core sampler implementation and unit tests - [x] Orchestrator finite-state machine + integration tests - [x] Perf microbenchmarks (latency of sampler decision < 50us) - [x] Observability: metrics, histograms, and events emitted - [x] Helm values and example configs - [x] Docs with rollout guidance Testing: unit and integration tests included under perf-canary/tests. Local load tests were run with scripts/loadtests/stratified_probe_runner.py against a staging canary. Perf results: average added CPU per probe: +0.9%, median decision latency: 18us (p95 42us). On a controlled noisy workload, the deferred fallback prevented 3/4 spurious rollbacks compared to baseline over a 4h window. Commits (summary): - feat(sampler): implement stratified cohort selector and budget accounting - feat(orchestrator): add deferred fallback FSM and escrow accounting - test: add unit and e2e tests for sampling and orchestrator - perf: microbench harness and measurement scripts - docs: operational guide and example configs - ci: add canary perf pipeline job Review notes: this is intentionally conservative with defaults to avoid changing behavior for existing installs. The stratified sampler exposes a simple metrics surface: canary_probe_count_total{cohort="..."}, canary_entropy_score, canary_escrow_state{state="pending|active|committed|aborted"}. Observability: added Prometheus metrics (observability/metrics/canary_metrics.prom) and a dashboard template in docs. Rollout plan: feature-flag on in staging for 48h, evaluate canary success rate and rollback count, then enable in limited production tenant slice (5%) for 72h with close monitoring, then scale up. Admin override: immediate forced-fallback endpoint available for on-call. Runtime considerations: sampler is written to be lock-free for fast path; budget accounting uses sharded counters to minimize contention. Known limitations: - sampling across many tiny tenants can dilute budgets; recommended to group low-volume tenants into 'micro' bucket - current entropy normalizer uses exponential smoothing; long-tail pattern shifts may need recalibration Future work: adaptive per-cohort thresholds based on historical variance, integration with traffic-curation probe scheduler for load shaping.

incident_context: Related to recent noisy rollback incident on 2025-12-09 (SUP-8123) where a transient cache miss in one region caused a 15-minute rollback; design here aims to prevent similar thrash by deferring decisions.
notes: This PR is intentionally conservative: feature remains opt-in and defaults mirror existing sampler. Operators should monitor canary_entropy_score and canary_escrow_state during rollout.
